## Purpose
The single `pydantic-settings`-backed `Settings` object read by nearly every backend subsystem: LLM provider selection (Bedrock/Anthropic/Mistral), SSE transport tuning, shutdown-drain budgets, sandbox/runtime limits, and security-sensitive boot-time validation of `SECRET_KEY` and `DATABASE_URL` logging.

## Shape
- `redact_db_url(url)` — strips any inline password from a DB URL before it can reach a logger (module docstring: this previously leaked live Postgres credentials into CloudWatch).
- `Settings(BaseSettings)` — one large flat settings class covering: LLM provider config (`ANTHROPIC_*`, `MISTRAL_*`, `BEDROCK_*`), token/timeout ceilings (`MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`, `LLM_CALL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`), SSE tuning (`SSE_KEEPALIVE_PING_SECONDS`, `SSE_SUBSCRIBER_QUEUE_MAXSIZE`), graceful-shutdown budgets (`SHUTDOWN_CONCIERGE_DRAIN_SECONDS`, `SHUTDOWN_STOP_RUNS`), sandbox/runtime limits (`RUNS_ROOT`, `AGENT_RECURSION_LIMIT`, `RUN_DIR_TTL_HOURS`), and core app config (`SECRET_KEY`, `DATABASE_URL`, `CORS_ORIGINS`).
- `_default_shutdown_stop_runs_from_env` (`model_validator`) — resolves `SHUTDOWN_STOP_RUNS`'s environment-differentiated default (True in dev, False elsewhere) only when the operator didn't set it explicitly.
- `_validate_secret_key` (`model_validator`) — refuses to boot (raises `SecretKeyMisconfigured`) if `SECRET_KEY` is empty, the shipped default, or under the minimum length, in any non-development `ENV`.
- Module-level `settings = Settings()` singleton, plus a small block that mirrors `LANGSMITH_*` settings into `os.environ` for LangChain's auto-detection.

## Why this shape
Nearly every field carries an inline comment explaining a specific incident or constraint it encodes (e.g. the CloudWatch credential leak behind `redact_db_url`, the arithmetic behind the shutdown-drain budget, the SIGTERM-vs-SIGINT reasoning behind `SHUTDOWN_STOP_RUNS`) — the file functions as both configuration and a documented decision log for values that were previously wrong in production.
